query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a minor amount (approximately 1–2 atomic%) of Nb to the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy will improve its long-term mechanical and environmental performance by modifying the phase-boundary chemistry. In particular, Nb will segregate to the lamellar interfaces to enhance cohesion and form stable nano‐precipitates that suppress creep deformation and corrosive attack under extreme thermal cycling.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA with a fine, dual-phase lamellar fcc/B2 (or fcc + L12 after low‐temperature annealing) microstructure produced by tailored thermo‐mechanical processing.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled, minor Nb addition (∼1–2 at.%) during alloy synthesis.
generation.conditions: Tested under conditions mimicking aircraft/spacecraft fasteners: accelerated thermal cycling (from cryogenic temperatures up to 900 °C), sustained mechanical loading (to simulate creep at room and elevated temperatures), and exposure to corrosive environments (e.g., chloride-containing sulfuric acid).
generation.structural_mediator: Nb segregation to phase boundaries leading to enhanced interfacial cohesion and the in-situ formation of Nb-rich nano-precipitates at the lamellar interfaces.
generation.mechanism: The Nb atoms preferentially segregate along the lamellar boundaries, thereby reinforcing them against microcrack initiation and diffusion-driven creep. Additionally, the formation of fine, stable Nb-rich precipitates within the fcc phase is expected to impede dislocation motion without reducing ductility excessively and simultaneously act as barriers to corrosive agents, which helps in stabilizing the passive film.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the undoped AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA, the Nb-doped variant will show an increase in yield strength (on the order of approximately 200 MPa or more), improved long-term creep resistance, and reduced corrosion rates under aggressive conditions while maintaining an acceptable balance of ductility.
generation.baseline: The state-of-the-art AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA processed by tailored thermo‐mechanical treatments that achieve enhanced strength–ductility synergy but still fall short of industrial performance requirements under long-term thermal and corrosive challenges.
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective only within a low doping range (∼1–2 at.% Nb) and under the specific thermal, mechanical, and corrosive conditions outlined; higher doping levels could lead to unwanted embrittlement or phase instability.
generation.uncertainty: This proposal builds on evidence that dopant additions (e.g., Y/Hf in coatings, PMC10488378) can modify high-temperature behavior and that nano-precipitation (PMC6478865) increases strength. However, extending these effects by using Nb specifically to enhance both creep resistance and corrosion protection in eutectic HEAs has not been demonstrated. The exact segregation behavior of Nb and its impact on both interfacial cohesion and passive film stability remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of standard AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA (control) and one set doped with 1–2 at.% Nb. Ensure both sets undergo identical casting and thermo-mechanical processing to develop comparable fine lamellar microstructures. Subject samples to accelerated thermal cycling (e.g., cycling between -50 °C and 900 °C), long-term creep tests under fixed loads at room temperature and elevated temperature, and corrosion tests in a chloride-containing sulfuric acid environment.
measurements: Mechanical tests: quasi-static and dynamic tensile and compressive tests to measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation.
Creep tests: monitoring strain versus time under constant load.
Corrosion tests: electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), potentiodynamic polarization, and weight loss measurements.
Microstructural analysis: SEM/TEM with EDS mapping to evaluate Nb segregation and nano-precipitate formation at phase boundaries.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-doped samples do not display statistically significant improvements—in particular, if there is less than approximately a 150–200 MPa increase in yield strength, no measurable decrease in creep strain rates, or if corrosion rates remain equal to or worse than the undoped alloy (or if ductility is substantially reduced)—then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractBoth crack-free AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) and Y and Hf co-doping AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA (YHf-EHEA) coatings were prepared by laser cladding. The solidification microstructure, thermal stability, and hot corrosion performance of the coatings at 900 °C under 75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl molten salts were investigated. The experimental results showed that the structure of the as-deposited coatings consisted of FCC and BCC/B2 phases. After heat treatment, an Al-rich L12 phase was precipitated in the FCC phase of all coatings. The grain sizes of the EHEA and YHf-EHEA coatings after heat treatment at 900 °C for 10 h increased by 27.5% and 15.7%, respectively, compared to the as-deposited coatings. Meanwhile, after hot corrosion, the spallation areas of the YHf-EHEA and EHEA coatings accounted for 14.98% and 5.67% of the total surface area, respectively. cited_evidence.text: The advantage of such a two-phase eutectic alloy is that it consists of a more easily deformable ductile (fcc or fcc + L12) phase, and a hard, difficult to deform, B2 + bcc phase. The hard B2 + bcc phase defines the inter-lamellar spacing of the softer fcc phase. To evaluate the mechanical performance of the Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy, the CR-H and CR-H-580 conditions were tested under two different strain rates (10−3 s−1 and 2 × 103 s−1) and the corresponding stress-strain plots are shown in Fig. 6. Figure 6(a) shows the engineering (thick line) and true (thin line) stress-strain plots from quasi-static testing. The CR-H condition with fcc + B2 (with fine scale bcc precipitates) shows a yield strength (YS) of ~770 MPa, UTS ~1090 MPa with an elongation to failure (EF) of ~17% under the quasi-static deformation (10−3). The CR-H-580 condition with the fcc + L12 & B2 + bcc microstructure exhibited a YS ~1080 MPa, UTS ~1370 MPa and EF of ~15%. A precipitation strengthening of ~310 MPa is observed after the additional heat treatment with just ~2% reduction in the elongation.
